abandon: The mechanism says the cued base's extra losses at T 1.0 are tail-token slips, and that a lower temperature would avoid them. The board already contradicts that cause. (1) result-faf15a located the first wrong step in 51 finished-wrong T 1.0 answers of the cued base and found that 'the base's wrong step is not an unlikely sample'. Those steps score 'log-prob -0.53 per token vs -0.63 for control text (W4 refuted)'. The item concludes: 'truncation or low temperature cannot remove these steps, which fits the min-p/top-p negatives'. A tail-token slip would score below control text, and lowering T or cutting the tail would remove it. (2) result-44b4df cut the tail directly at T 1.0 and found 'No truncation rule beats untruncated sampling on MATH-500 at T 1.0': 'base top-p 0.95 -0.2 [-3.8, 3.2]' and 'base min-p 0.1 -1.2 pts [-4.6, 2.2]'. The tail-slip cause predicts a gain there, at least on short problems where loops do not return. (3) The observation the mechanism was built to explain has a simpler reading. In knowledge-13cff3, 'on the 402 problems that finish at T 0.6, T 1.0 gets 361-364 against 378'. That subset is chosen by the T 0.6 sample's own outcome: its finished answers are '94 %' right. Selecting on T 0.6's own outcome favours T 0.6 even when both temperatures have the same per-problem accuracy, so the number does not show a second item axis or a short-problem crossover. The mechanism's cause is contradicted, and its target fact is explained by selection, so a theory built on it would waste tests.
